summary: Modoc NF lookout: 1930 steel tower (30 ft, Region 5 4AR design) on a new Forest Service road; 1940 fire and 2001 vandalism; 2025 relocation or restoration talks ongoing.

facts.design: California Region 5 4AR design on a 30-foot steel tower, with an all-glass cab (NHLR; 1932 newspaper)
facts.status_note: Standing, but the cabin is open to the weather and deteriorating, per NHLR
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Modoc National Forest

staffing.status: volunteers may staff it in summer (2007 photo note); no current staffing confirmed

visit.trail_note: No source read confirms public access or the road's status today; the 1930 road was built to give auto access to the summit

events.note: Sugar hill fire burned over 8,000 acres of timber; forest lookout D.M. Miller was dazed by smoke and wandered for hours
Work on the steel tower began September 1930; NHLR gives 1930/31
Forest Service road to the summit completed by July 1930, giving auto access; the summit had been reached only by a steep pack trail
Steel tower in service; it replaced a tree platform that had served for about a decade
Keith Wells stationed on the lookout since June 1931, per a January 1932 newspaper
Forest Service telephone line under construction from a camp to the Sugar Hill lookout
Hess Ranch fire in July 1940 spread into the old 1929 burn; the lookout had to be removed from the tower
Forest Service plan lists a standard lookout on a tower, with garage and woodshed, water storage and latrine
General inspection: shutters and catwalk should be replaced because of dry rot
Vandals broke the windows, pulled off wooden shutters, and destroyed the furniture and most of the interior paneling (reported June 27, 2001)
Photo caption: fair condition; wooden cab needs repair and paint, steel tower good
Report author met forest staff at the lookout; relocation or restoration ideas discussed; project status ongoing

corrections.why: NHLR gives a 30-foot steel tower, and the 1930 newspaper plan says the tower would be 30 feet high (about 9.1 m). No source read gives a height near 95 m, which would be about 313 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1930/31. Work on the steel tower began in September 1930, and a 1932 newspaper says a lookout had been posted there since June 1931. The story gives 1930 for the start of work and notes NHLR's range.

A 1930 newspaper describes the earlier tree platform as a little over 60 feet high. The steel tower was planned at 30 feet. The story uses the 30-foot steel tower height and does not give the platform height.
NHLR gives 7,276 ft (2,218 m). A Peakbagging photo page gives 7,267 ft. The brief's 2217.7 m fits NHLR; the story does not give an elevation.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 95.4 is wrong; the tower is 30 feet (9.1 m) per NHLR and the 1930 plan, so the record is corrected. Access is unknown: no source read confirms whether the summit road or the lookout is open to the public today, so no access level is set and the story says to check with the Modoc National Forest. Staffing has no current source; the last mention is a 2007 photo note about possible summer volunteers. The 2025 Cal-North report says forest staff and the report author discussed relocation or restoration; no decision is recorded. The 1929 fire is named for Sugar hill, but the sources read do not say whether it reached the summit. Facebook group posts found in search were not used. No photos added.
